test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 28 Nov, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is NOT a Directive Principle of State Policy?

options.text: Valuing the rich heritage of our culture
Uniform civil code for the citizens

solution:
The correct answer is __**Valuing the rich heritage of our culture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, laid down in Part IV of the Constitution of India.
 
• The DPSPs aim to establish a just society in India and are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• Promotion of co-operative societies, Uniform civil code for the citizens, and Separation of judiciary from executive are examples of Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• Valuing the rich heritage of our culture is not listed as a Directive Principle of State Policy but is mentioned in the Fundamental Duties under Article 51A(f) of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy:**

 
 
• They are inspired by the Directive Principles given in the Constitution of Ireland.
 
• They aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They emphasize the welfare state model of governance.
 
• These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• Fundamental Duties are listed under Article 51A in Part IVA of the Constitution of India.
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• There are 11 Fundamental Duties prescribed for every citizen of India.
 
• They are meant to serve as a constant reminder to citizens about their duties towards the nation.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Civil Code:**
 
 
• It refers to the proposal to replace personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community in India with a common set governing every citizen.
 
• Article 44 of the Directive Principles of State Policy sets its implementation as a goal.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Judiciary from Executive:**
 
 
• It ensures the independence of the judiciary from the executive branch of the government.
 
• This principle is enshrined in Article 50 of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
